image_description: A medium shot of a three-piece band performing on an elevated stage. From left to right: a guitarist with long hair playing a sunburst electric guitar, a bassist in the center playing a white bass guitar, and a lead singer on the right holding a microphone. The background features a large banner with graffiti-style art and partial text. Stage monitors (speakers) are visible at the bottom edge.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elevated rectangular platform, raised slightly above floor level.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The subjects are clearly standing on a raised surface relative to the implied audience level, indicated by the angle of the stage monitors at their feet.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dimensions vary from small intimate platforms to large theatrical stages spanning the full width of a performance hall.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frame is cropped tightly on the performers; the full width and depth of the stage are not visible, making dimensional assessment impossible.
The line where the stage floor meets the vertical drop (obscured by monitors) is visually distinct, defining the performance boundary.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface is covered with matte black flooring or painted wood.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The floor beneath the musicians' feet appears to be a dark, non-reflective material consistent with standard stage decking.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Steps or ramps provide access from floor level.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Access points are outside the camera's field of view.
The top of the image cuts off just above the performers' heads; overhead rigging is not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Constructed from wood or metal decking.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the specific material grain is hard to see due to lighting/resolution, the structural rigidity implies standard wood/metal construction.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface shows scuff marks from performances.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The resolution and lighting conditions prevent the identification of fine surface details like scuff marks.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Side and rear may have wings or backdrop supports.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A large backdrop/banner is visible behind the band, supported by vertical truss structures on the sides.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The white lettering on the black background (appearing to start with 'C') is malformed and lacks clear character definition, typical of AI struggling with text rendering.
The fingers on the fretboard appear slightly fused and lack distinct joint definition, though it is subtle due to motion blur simulation.
The connection between the neck and the headstock of the bass guitar appears slightly warped and indistinct.

selected_experts.reason: To verify if the scene context (lighting, crowd implication, equipment) aligns with the 'stage' class label versus a generic room or studio.
To audit the anatomical correctness of the three human figures, specifically checking for extra limbs or fused fingers which are common AI artifacts in complex poses.
To rigorously analyze the gibberish text observed on the backdrop, determining if it is illegible noise or failed character generation.
To check for fusion artifacts between the musicians' hands and the guitars/bass, ensuring distinct object boundaries.

focus_areas: Anatomical integrity of hands and fingers interacting with instruments
Legibility and structure of background text
Structural logic of musical instruments (neck-to-body connections)
Boundary separation between performers and the backdrop
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'text_gibberish' artifact. In real concert photos, out-of-focus text might look blurry, but AI text often has 'melted' character shapes. Differentiate between optical blur and generative failure. Also, verify if the 'pose_auditor' flags any asymmetry in the number of fingers, as this is a high-risk area for this composition.
